drafts.title: Tesla Model 3 RWD still leases like a mid-$500s payment once you amortize.
drafts.window: 11 AM-1 PM MT Wednesday (late morning-afternoon OK). Soft-pedal "post at 8am."
drafts.angle: Electrek manufacturer table: Model 3 RWD about $419/mo for 36 months with $4,364 due (effective ~$529), 10,000 mi/yr. Soft-pedal Tue Bolt $419 twin and Mon Prologue/EV3 by stressing Tesla badge + factory nationwide sticky note. Kitchen-table: the advertised monthly is not the payment that hits your budget.
bullets: Electrek manufacturer table (Sep update): Tesla Model 3 RWD ~$419/mo, 36 mo, $4,364 due, 10,000 mi/yr; avg monthly cost ~$529; MSRP ~$38,630.
Same Electrek ladder: Model 3 Premium RWD ~$429 / $4,374 due (~$539 avg); Model 3 Premium AWD ~$499 / $4,444 due (~$609 avg).
Soft-pedal Tue Bolt LT factory $419/$5,119 (~$550) twin and Mon Prologue/EV3/IONIQ5 lease ladder.
Soft-pedal Manheim used-EV price-wave framing.
Confirm live Tesla Current Offers / VIN sheet before signing; taxes and fees vary by state.
drafts.body:
A $419 Model 3 monthly looks clean until you write the due on a sticky note.

Electrek's factory line still shows a Model 3 RWD around $419 a month for 36 months with about $4,364 due. Average that drive-off and you are nearer $529 a month before tax. That is a different kitchen-table conversation than a website monthly with no due, and a different conversation than a used-EV price ticker.

US kitchen-table take for a 40-year-old commuting EV shopper, or a 58-year-old who wants a boring payment stack:

1) Ask for the out-the-door sheet on the exact Model 3 VIN, not a website monthly.
2) Divide due-at-signing by months, then add the payment. That is your real lease number.
3) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
4) Map weekday Level 2 at home, work, or a real apartment plan if you rent.
5) Confirm miles/year. A 10,000-mile line can sting if you drive more.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "amortize the due" math on a mainstream EV.

55+ line: a mid-$500s effective lease only helps if insurance and the plug plan keep your independence.

Electrek still shows an Ioniq 9 S around $399 a month for 36 months with about $4,999 due. Average that and you are nearer $527 a month before tax. You are shopping a family hauler, not a small hatch. That is a different kitchen-table conversation than a two-row IONIQ 5 payment, and a different conversation than a big SUV sticker with no lease math.

US kitchen-table take:

1) Pull the out-the-door sheet on the exact Ioniq 9 VIN.
2) Amortize the $4,999. Write the effective monthly.
3) Quote insurance on that VIN. Three-row EVs are not automatically cheap to insure.
4) Confirm third-row reality for your household, not the brochure photo.
5) Map a real Level 2 plan before you fall in love with the cabin.

drafts.title: Illinois Solar for All still lets income-eligible renters subscribe without a roof.
drafts.window: 11 AM-1 PM MT Wednesday (late morning-afternoon OK). Soft-pedal "post at 8am."
drafts.angle: Illinois Solar for All Community Solar: income-eligible renters and homeowners at or under ~80% Area Median Income can subscribe to a project in their utility territory and are designed to pay less than without the subscription. Soft-pedal Tue Maryland CS, Mon Rockford, Sun CPS, Tue leftover Ann Arbor. Kitchen-table: apartment solar credits without landlord panels.
bullets: Illinois Solar for All Community Solar: income-eligible renters and homeowners can participate; household income at or under 80% of Area Median Income (AMI); projects must be in the subscriber's utility territory.
Program design: Approved Vendors develop projects and pass savings so participants are structured to pay less for electricity than without the subscription.

LIHEAP referral path: Illinois Solar for All partners with DCEO Office of Community Assistance so LIHEAP-verified households can skip duplicate income verification and get paired with a subscription manager.
Households that do not qualify for ILSFA can look at Illinois Shines community solar instead.
Illinois Shines Program Year 2026-27 opened with ~1,000 MW of capacity; community solar max project size raised from 5 MW to 10 MW under CRGA updates (IPA June 2026).
drafts.body:
You do not need a roof you own to get a solar line on the bill in Illinois.

Illinois Solar for All still runs a Community Solar path for income-eligible renters and homeowners. The income screen is roughly 80% of Area Median Income. The project has to sit in your utility territory. The point of the program is simple kitchen-table math: the subscription is supposed to leave you paying less than you would without it.

US kitchen-table take for a 42-year-old renter in ComEd or Ameren territory, or a 60-year-old on a fixed income:

1) Check whether you are income-eligible for Illinois Solar for All, not a random Facebook solar ad.
2) If you already use LIHEAP, ask your local LIHEAP agency about the referral path so you are not redoing paperwork twice.
3) Ask for the dollar savings in writing: monthly credit, subscription fee, cancellation rules.
4) Confirm the project is in your utility territory before you sign.
5) If you are over the ILSFA income line, look at Illinois Shines community solar instead of walking away from solar entirely.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "renter solar with a written savings floor."

55+ line: a community solar credit only helps if the fine print keeps your independence.

drafts.title: UK homeowners can finance solar+battery over 2-10 years at 9.9% APR. US lesson: shop the loan.
drafts.window: 11 AM-1 PM MT Wednesday (late morning-afternoon OK). Soft-pedal "post at 8am."
drafts.angle: Sep 22, 2026: UK distributor Segen + Zopa Bank launch residential solar/storage finance. Representative 9.9% APR, terms 24-120 months, full install (equipment, labour, scaffolding) via installer Proposal Tool. Soft-pedal Tue leftover AU solar+EV tax story by stressing finance sticky note. Kitchen-table: the APR and term matter as much as the wattage.
bullets: pv magazine (Sep 22, 2026): Segen launches residential solar+battery financing with Zopa Bank; representative 9.9% APR; terms 2-10 years (24-120 months).

Segen UK: Segen Finance acts as credit broker; Zopa Bank is the lender; finance integrates into Segen Proposal Tool; personalized quote in ~2 minutes with soft check / no score impact on initial quote per Segen.
Financing can cover full installation cost including equipment, labour, and scaffolding; historically UK residential solar often required full upfront cash.
Segen note: homeowners without ~GBP 10,000 (~$13,300) "lying around" are the next tranche the product aims to unlock (Walker via pv magazine).
Warm Home Loans subsidy may later lower rates; sign-ups before that program goes live are not retroactively adjusted (Segen/pv magazine).
drafts.body:
Panels are only half the kitchen-table math. The loan is the other half.

This week UK distributor Segen and digital lender Zopa Bank opened residential solar and battery financing at a representative 9.9% APR for terms from 24 to 120 months. The quote lives inside the installer's proposal tool. The loan can cover equipment, labour, and scaffolding. That matters because a lot of UK households knew solar helped the bill but did not have five figures sitting in checking.

US kitchen-table take for a Grand Junction roof shopper, or any US household comparing cash vs loan vs lease:

1) Ask for the APR, term, and total interest in writing, not just "low monthly."
2) Compare cash vs loan vs PPA/lease on the same system size.
3) Confirm what happens if you sell the house mid-term.
4) Quote insurance and any HOA rules before you sign.
5) Do not let a pretty production estimate hide a expensive finance stack.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "shop the loan like you shop the panels."

55+ line: a 10-year solar loan only helps if the payment stays boring on a fixed income.

drafts.title: EVgo is adding Tesla V4 Superchargers with Magic Dock. Trip-plan the network, not just the badge.
drafts.window: 11 AM-1 PM MT Wednesday (late morning-afternoon OK). Soft-pedal "post at 8am."
drafts.angle: EVgo Aug 5, 2026: deploying "EVgo Superchargers" (Tesla V4) up to 500 kW / 1,000 V with Magic Dock; appear in Tesla nav / Trip Planner; first sites 2H 2026; up to ~200 miles in 15 minutes claimed. Soft-pedal IONNA LIVE and EA Pass+ LIVE. Kitchen-table: more NACS choices on road trips without adapter drama.
bullets: EVgo press release (Aug 5, 2026): plans to install EVgo Superchargers (Tesla V4) capable of up to 500 kW / 1,000 V across its metropolitan network.
Magic Dock: CCS or NACS vehicles can charge natively without an adapter; longer cables called out for inlet location flexibility.
Tesla navigation / Trip Planner: EVgo Superchargers will appear in-car; Tesla drivers can be auto-routed; deployments start fall 2026; first sites expected operational 2H 2026.
Demand context: EVgo cites consumer demand up over 700% in three years; more than 35 NACS-equipped models anticipated by end of 2026; more than 3 million Tesla vehicles already sold in the US.
Network footprint note: EVgo says more than 1,200 fast charging stations across 47 states (company about blurb). Soft-pedal IONNA stall-count and EA Pass+ membership math (both LIVE).
drafts.body:
Road-trip charging is getting less tribal. That is good for household budgets.

EVgo is adding Tesla V4 Superchargers to its own network, branded EVgo Superchargers, at up to 500 kW and 1,000 volts, with Magic Dock so CCS or NACS cars can plug without an adapter. Those stalls are supposed to show up in Tesla navigation and the Trip Planner. First sites are aimed at the second half of 2026. EVgo says the hardware can add up to about 200 miles in 15 minutes when conditions cooperate.

US kitchen-table take for a 45-year-old planning I-70 miles, or a 62-year-old who hates dead-end chargers:

1) Before a trip, open more than one charging app. Compare price, idle fees, and live availability.
2) If you drive NACS, note which non-Tesla networks now speak your plug language.
3) If you still use CCS, confirm Magic Dock or adapter rules before you leave.
4) Watch idle fees. A cheap kWh rate is not cheap if you sit through lunch.
5) Soft-pedal any one network loyalty story. Households need options.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save "trip-plan the network, not the brand war."

55+ line: more open stalls only help if the price and idle rules stay boring.
